A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same faithfulness research despite substantial retitling and refocusing. All 23 pages of v1 and 13 pages of v2, including their appendices, provide readable text, equations, figures and tables supporting comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original surrogate comparisons, U-CBEM evaluations, optimization experiments, OOD and adversarial tests, and additional empirical analyses in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 reports original controlled metric comparisons, three-task benchmarking, concept-count experiments and adversarial evaluations in Tables 3–5 and Figure 2.

M1.justification: v2 removes v1's spatial-distribution component and the Optimally Faithful (OF) procedure for learning concepts, importances and spatial weights. Its SURF surrogate instead uses each U-CBEM's projection operation P and concept importances, including nonlinear projections, rather than v1's prescribed inner products. The method is explicitly restricted to the final linear layer; MAE and EMD remain.

E1.justification: v2 retains Caltech-101 classification and adds CelebA multi-attribute prediction and UTK-Face age regression. It removes the Fashion-MNIST, DTD and Omniglot OOD evaluations reported in v1 Section 6.3.1 and Appendix H.1. These changes substantially alter the evaluated tasks and represented data.

E2.justification: The benchmark drops standalone K-Means, NMF and PCA comparisons and adds evaluated MCD results; MCD was only cited in v1. CDISCO, ICE, CRAFT and ConceptSHAP remain, with ConceptSHAP renamed C-SHAP. The surrogate comparison removes the PACE-derived logistic regressor, adds ICE-Eval, and evaluates both cross-entropy and L1-trained C-SHAP-Eval variants.

E3.justification: v1's main classification experiment uses ResNet-50 without global pooling and 49 concepts; its appendix also evaluates pooled ResNet-50 with one concept. v2 uses pooled ResNet-50 with five concepts for benchmarking. It adds randomized controls, rank correlation and normalized-L1 measurements. PGD now maximizes changes in the model's predictions instead of disagreement between surrogate and model, materially changing the attack protocol.

E4.justification: v2 expands the perfect-explanation check with randomized-importance and fully random controls, adds concept-count sensitivity curves, and redesigns adversarial robustness analysis. It removes v1's importance/spatial-learning ablations, weight-alignment analysis, deletion-strategy and off-manifold diagnostics, OOD robustness tests and qualitative failure cases from Appendices B, C, H and I.

E5.justification: v1 reports image-level means and standard deviations for adversarial errors. v2 instead reports paired differences and introduces one-sided paired t-tests at p < 0.01, with nonsignificant entries suppressed. It also newly reports averaging the metric-comparison results over ten seeds, without seed variability. This establishes new replication reporting, not an explicit increase over a known earlier run count.

E6.justification: v1's OF results, including 0.269 MAE and 0.023 EMD in Table 2, and its OOD result tables disappear. v2 reports new results including MCD's 1.42 MAE/0.079 EMD on classification and CDISCO's 32.6-year regression MAE, alongside new randomization, concept-count and adversarial findings. Changed methods and settings prevent treating these as direct performance gains or losses.

T1.justification: v1 Appendix F's constrained optimization formulations and convex reparameterization arguments are removed, together with Appendix J's spatial-surrogate derivation and spatial probability constraints. v2 retains the basic normalized linear-layer identity in Equation 9, but formulates explanations through P and adds the MCD subspace decomposition in Appendix B.8. This substantially changes the mathematical scope.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion abandon claims about spatial awareness, OF's improvement over prior methods and OF's OOD generalization. v2 instead claims a unified treatment of faithfulness measures, controlled validation of SURF, the first comprehensive U-CBEM faithfulness benchmark, and applications to concept-count selection and adversarial robustness. The broad concern about unfaithful explanations remains.

C2.justification: v2 develops failure explanations involving cross-class reconstruction, nonlinear projections and importance-score completeness, and explains MCD's advantage through multidimensional concepts. It adds interpretations of concept-count plateaus and differing logit/probability responses to attacks. v1's interpretations concerning learned spatial information, OF generalization and OF's unresolved interpretability tradeoff disappear; the final-layer restriction remains explicit.

D1.justification: v2 newly documents Caltech-101's 80/20 split, CelebA subsampling, UTK-Face stratification and ViT fine-tuning, projection implementations, and MCD's 10,000-embedding cap. It removes OF optimization instructions and v1's explicit logit-shift correction documentation; omission does not establish whether that correction was discontinued. The abstract adds a future code-release statement, without establishing an actual release.

R1.justification: v2 repositions the work around evaluation unification and benchmarking rather than a new explanation algorithm. It expands discussion of previously cited MCD, adds a dedicated concept-bottleneck-model distinction and cognitive-psychology references motivating parsimony, and removes PACE discussion and the supervised-CBEM appendix. These are substantive positioning changes beyond reference renumbering.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction and conclusion are extensively rewritten, and SF is renamed SURF. A new preliminaries section precedes related work, while metric discussion is reorganized around a taxonomy and desiderata. The experimental narrative and appendices are substantially rebuilt, beyond changes attributable solely to added results.

P2.justification: v2 adds metric-taxonomy tables, a grouped three-setting comparison, a three-task benchmark table and concept-count plots. The retained pipeline diagram is revised and renumbered, with spatial information removed. v1's motivation diagram, spatial-learning and OOD tables, diagnostic plots and qualitative image panels disappear, substantially changing the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: v2's clearer evaluation focus, randomized controls, MCD comparison and new prediction tasks strengthen its validation. However, it removes empirical support for retained deletion-metric criticisms from v1 Appendix C and loses OOD robustness evidence. Its new statistical reporting is also unclear: Table 5 retains negative differences despite describing one-sided tests for increases and suppression of nonsignificant entries. These benefits and losses leave the net quality direction uncertain.
